result.title: HoMe: Toward Practical Harness Optimization of Memory Systems for AI Assistants
result.summary: The behavior of memory systems for long-running AI assistants is governed by a harness, which consists of the code, prompts, and configurations for memory construction, maintenance, retrieval, and answer generation. However, optimizing the harness of a memory system remains largely manual, and unrestricted editing alone does not ensure structural improvements. In this paper, we introduce HoMe, an evaluation-driven framework that iteratively evaluates candidate harnesses and derives each new candidate from any previously evaluated harness by editing any part of it. HoMe combines session-level memory versioning with execution traces to identify shared failure mechanisms across cases and localize them to the responsible sessions and harness components. It encourages early structural exploration through candidate gating and reduces evaluation cost through smoke tests, adaptive sampling, and the reuse of constructed memory. We validate HoMe with the open-source memory system ReMe on two large-scale long-horizon memory benchmarks, LongMemEval-S and BEAM. With six formal candidate evaluations per benchmark, after a full initial evaluation, HoMe discovers harnesses that improve end-task performance over the originally strong harness while consuming far fewer query-time tokens. The code is available at https://github.com/agentscope-ai/ReMe.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 HoMe，一个评估驱动的 harness 优化框架：迭代评测候选 harness 并对其任意部分（记忆构建、维护、检索、答案生成）进行编辑，借助会话级记忆版本与执行轨迹定位跨案例的共享失败机制，并用 smoke test、自适应采样和记忆复用来压低评估成本，在 LongMemEval-S 与 BEAM 上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「候选 harness 迭代评测 + 失败机制定位 + 低成本筛选」流程，可能可供核查地迁移到 VLM 推理中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 控制策略与证据获取流程的自动优化；但论文自身不涉及视觉输入或 latent 状态，联系仅为方法论层面。
